claims.text: The proposed MTP would be trained on high-temperature ab initio data from elemental, binary, and multicomponent refractory-alloy simulations.
The MTP will capture many-body interactions in disordered refractory-HEA liquids more accurately than the EAM reference.
The MTP will capture high-temperature local atomic distortions in the disordered liquid.
Using the MTP reference will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
The MTP will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 25–40% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The target material class includes TiZrTaHfNb-like refractory HEAs in both solid and liquid states.
Approximately 2200–3200 K is the relevant near-melting temperature range for the stated refractory HEAs.
MTPs use moment-tensor descriptors and basis functions that depend on local atomic neighborhoods.
Moment-tensor descriptors quantify local anisotropy and distortion under high-temperature conditions.
The proposed MTP contains higher-order interaction terms that are absent from the EAM baseline.
Those higher-order terms will provide a better representation of the heterogeneous energy landscape of the liquid.
Adding multicomponent HEA ab initio configurations to training will mitigate extrapolation risk.
The MTP-based free energies should agree with full ab initio values to within approximately 5 meV/atom.
TOR-TILD's traditional EAM references rely on pairwise potentials.
TOR-TILD's EAM references fail to capture crucial many-body effects in high-temperature refractory-HEA liquids.
Applicability is limited to refractory HEAs compositionally similar to TiZrTaHfNb and temperatures of approximately 2200–3200 K.
Underrepresentation of rare liquid configurations may cause residual free-energy discrepancies.
Transfer of training information from elemental and binary systems to a full multicomponent HEA remains uncertain.
The proposed benchmark compares MTP thermodynamic-integration free energies with full ab initio results for identical solid and liquid conditions across the specified temperature range.
The hypothesis is falsified if the free-energy deviation exceeds 5 meV/atom or the error reduction relative to the EAM reference is less than 25%.
